message.content:
Keysight Technologies Inc reported revenue of 1.85 billion for the quarter ended 2026-07-31, up 36.54 per cent from a year earlier and 7.51 per cent from the quarter before, with net income of 397 million and a net margin of 21.51 per cent [D1]. The Communications Solutions Group generated revenue of 1.35 billion, up 43.09 per cent, and operating income of 458 million, up 86.18 per cent, while the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group generated revenue of 501 million, up 21.60 per cent, and operating income of 155 million, up 68.48 per cent [D1]. Total assets were 11.92 billion, stockholders' equity was 6.57 billion and net debt was 141 million [D1]. Guidance for the next quarter is revenue of 1.93 billion to 1.95 billion and earnings per share of 3.34 to 3.40 on a diluted share count of 172 million, with the mid point of the revenue range representing growth of 37 per cent [D1].

The shares closed at 333.42, above the 20 day average of 330.47, the 50 day average of 326.21 and the 200 day average of 289.31, in an uptrend state [D2]. The argument in the market is about durability rather than about the quarter, because demand is being driven by rapid scaling of the AI infrastructure ecosystem, wireline orders more than doubled year on year and wireline revenue exceeded wireless for the first time [D3]. The counter argument is supply, since management said the supply chain will remain the governor of near term revenue, that the supply environment is less flexible than a year ago and that converting demand into revenue is likely to be nonlinear [D3]. Management also flagged that one-time tariff impacts lifted fiscal 2026 profitability and will not repeat [D3]. Analyst tone on the call was slightly negative to pressing, with repeated questions about whether demand is sustainable and whether the outlook is capped by supply [D3]. Sell-side price targets point above the current level, but such targets are frequently set for reasons other than a genuine view of where the shares will trade and should be treated with caution [D5].

The plan is therefore to treat the guided fourth quarter as the first checkpoint, requiring revenue of 1.93 billion to 1.95 billion and earnings per share of 3.34 to 3.40 to be delivered [D1]. The second checkpoint is evidence that component supply is loosening enough to convert demand into revenue, since management calls supply the governor of near term revenue [D3]. The third is that margins hold without the one-time tariff benefit that flattered fiscal 2026 [D3]. On the tape, immediate resistance sits at 366.41 and the immediate support zone runs from 311.27 to 332.78 at a strength of 18 [D2].
